correctness.rationale: Examined normalization carefully: S consists only of hub o and leaves v_i, with d(o,vi)=rho and d(vi,vj)=2rho, and sum-normalized BL norm = sup|f|+Lip(f). Because μ(total)=0, put y_i=f(vi)-f(o) and translate f to center its entire range; the least sup norm is (U+V)/2 with U=max(0,-inf_i y_i), V=max(0,sup_i y_i). The exact Lip constant is sup_i |y_i|/rho because leaf-leaf differences <=2sup|y_i|. Homogeneity fixes max(U,V)=1, and pairing coefficients bounds |∫f dμ| by PV+QU, valid for countable absolutely summable series. Along edges U=1 and V=1 the fractional functions have derivatives of constant sign, so only three corners matter and give rho(P+Q)/(1+rho), 2rho P/(2+rho), 2rho Q/(2+rho). Explicit centered sign potential and two one-sided potentials attain each candidate even with infinitely many leaves; check the zero family separately. Comparing values gives exact transition at ratio (1+2/rho), with ties at equalities. Independently solved sixteen finite signed examples and four arm radii by a separate linear program (all agreement within 1e-8), including balanced, unbalanced and mixed-sign coefficients; analytic proof, not LP sampling, handles arbitrary countable I.
residual_risks: The point set excludes interior points of edges; replacing by a full real-tree star requires its own proof.
The sum-normalized BL norm must not be silently exchanged for max-normalized Fortet-Mourier convention.

value.rationale: Dudley/Fortet–Mourier is a canonical dual norm controlling convergence of signed finite or countable measures. An exact all-radius phase diagram on a natural star metric identifies when balanced sign potentials versus one-sided potentials are extremal, with nontrivial mass-imbalance transition 1+2/rho and explicit infinite-star attainment. This is a motivated sharp norm computation beyond a generic finite LP recipe or a single trivial molecule, even though it is special to equal arm lengths.
residual_risks: No unequal-arm version, nonzero-mass extension, or general tree metric formula asserted.

final_claim: For finite or countably infinite equal-arm star metric with arm length rho>0 and real absolutely summable zero-total-mass coefficient sequence a_i, the dual sum-normalized bounded-Lipschitz norm is max{rho(P+Q)/(rho+1),2rho max(P,Q)/(rho+2)}, with exact sharp switch of optimizers at P=(1+2/rho)Q or Q=(1+2/rho)P.
limitations: Sum normalization and real functions are essential; countable I requires absolutely summable coefficients.
